evidence.location: §4 LH1-C10 (line 370), against §0 R0.8 (lines 115-117), §10 D4 (line 481) and LH1-C14 (line 370)
evidence.observation: LH1-C10 opens 'each limit at its ceiling stays within the spec's time bound' but then enumerates only five of D4's seven limits: 'inputs at each roster ceiling load, with the input cap raised as they need; a source at the input-cap ceiling, a response at the response-cap ceiling and a budget at its ceiling each run; a route that reaches the timeout refuses within the timeout plus its grace'. D4 parameterizes seven caps, including 'route output (1 MiB, 16 MiB), retained file (128 KiB, today's read of a run's own files; ceiling 64 MiB)', and R0.8 binds 'Each cap that becomes a parameter has a hard maximum fixed in its spec, and a time-bound test at that maximum (standing rule 2)'. No criterion names a time-bound test at the retained-file (64 MiB) or route-output (16 MiB) ceiling: LH1-C14 only has the cap 'raised to fit' ('a run at the response and roster ceilings, with the retained-file cap raised to fit, completes'), which is not the ceiling, and the route-output cap appears in no demonstration at all.

concerns.recommendation: Name the retained-file and route-output ceilings in LH1-C10's demonstrations (or say explicitly that they share one of the listed bound tests and why), so R0.8's per-cap time-bound test is measured for all seven limits rather than five.
concerns.title: LH1-C10's enumerated ceiling tests cover five of D4's seven parameterized caps

evidence.location: §3 'Order' paragraph (lines 357-359), against the completion predicates (lines 71-77) and H25 (line 155)
evidence.observation: Section 3 pins the start condition to one commit: 'Start condition: `main` at `4ad0d216`, which holds IR1, so LH3's fixture can be an include root.' But the completion predicates state 'The whole-repository `uv run ruff check` exited 1 at `4ad0d216`' (line 71; H25 repeats 'the whole-repository `uv run ruff check` exited 1 at `4ad0d216` with 198 findings') and 'The re-sync is committed with this plan, so LH1 starts from a `main` where the whole repository lints clean `(p1)`' (lines 75-77). Both cannot hold: at exactly `4ad0d216` the whole-repository lint exits 1, so a lint-clean main at LH1 start is necessarily a later commit that carries the plan's own re-sync, not `4ad0d216` itself.

concerns.recommendation: Reword the section 3 start condition to name the state LH1 actually starts from, e.g. 'main at the plan-gate merge whose parent is `4ad0d216` (which holds IR1) plus the committed re-sync', so the pinned start commit and the claimed lint-clean start no longer conflict.
concerns.title: §3's start condition ('main at 4ad0d216') contradicts the lint-clean main the re-sync commit creates
